description: Write the SELECT of an incremental load that inserts new events from a staging table into a deduplicated target. The run processes staging rows whose ingested_at falls in the 3-day lookback window [@run_date - 2 days at 00:00 UTC, @run_date + 1 day at 00:00 UTC), with @run_date = DATE '2025-06-03'. Rules: (1) rows with NULL event_id are rejected; (2) within the window keep one row per event_id, the one with the earliest ingested_at; (3) do not emit events whose event_id already exists in the target, regardless of how old their event_ts is; (4) late-arriving events (event_ts before the window) that are not yet in the target must be emitted. Output columns: event_id (STRING), user_id (INT64), event_ts (TIMESTAMP), ingested_at (TIMESTAMP). Sort by event_id.

event_id.description: Producer-assigned id; can repeat on redelivery; occasionally NULL

event_ts.description: UTC time the event happened on the device

ingested_at.description: UTC arrival time; the table is partitioned on DATE(ingested_at)

event_ts.description: UTC event time; the table is partitioned on DATE(event_ts)

edge_cases: e1 was already loaded two days ago and is redelivered in the current window
e2 happened two weeks before the window but arrives now (late event) and must be loaded
e3 is duplicated inside the same window; the earliest arrival wins
e5 was ingested before the lookback window and is not this run's responsibility
common_failure_modes: FM2: Filtering the window on event_ts instead of ingested_at drops late-arriving e2 forever
FM1: Restricting the target lookup to the same recent event_ts partitions (for pruning) misses older duplicates, re-inserting already-loaded events
FM5: NOT IN against target ids misbehaves with NULL event_id; NULL ids also collapse into one 'duplicate' group if not rejected first
